statement: Let k be a finitely generated extension of the original field C, and let ∆0 be a central division algebra over k of degree e0. Fix an integer b ≥ 2, a k-vector space U of dimension at least three, and a subspace W ⊆ Symb (U∨ ), s = dimk W, such that every nonzero member of Wk̄ has an irreducible factor of multiplicity one. Choose integers h, M in this order, with h ≥ max {2} ∪ { vp(e0)s(pvp(b) − 1) : p | e0 }  , M ≥ 2h + 4s + 10. (6.1) Here vp is the p-adic valuation, and the prime-indexed set is empty if e0 = 1. Define Y = ( (ℓ1, . . . , ℓM ) ∈ U⊕M : M X m=1 w(ℓm) = 0 (w ∈ W) ) , X = P(Y ). Take the curve C, group G, and linearized line bundle L of Proposition 5.1 for this b. Write e = |G| = bb and gT = b − 1, and put B = M Y m=2 Pic0 (C), H = GM−1 , e1 = |H|. All products and curves here are over k, and H acts on the corresponding Picard factors by transport from the curve. Choose arbitrary characters ρ1, . . . , ρM : H → µb, and let H act on the points of the m-th block of Y by ρm. Let R be an affine space with a faithful linear H-action. Set K = k(B × X × R), F = KH . For the generic tuple of degree-zero line bundles Am, let E = M O m=2 H0 (CK, Am ⊗ LgT ). 24 Transport induces a semilinear H-action on EndK(E). Its fixed algebra ∆1 = EndK(E)H is central simple of degree e1 over F, and ∆ = (∆0 ⊗k F) ⊗F ∆1 (6.2) is a central division algebra of degree e0e1. Its scalar extension to K identifies with ∆0 ⊗k EndK(E); in the corresponding descent action, H fixes ∆0 pointwise.
